beginner.headline: Pornhub Age Checks Under Investigation
beginner.brief: Pornhub is a website that is being investigated. A regulator called Ofcom is checking the website's age system. Ofcom worries that children can still see adult content online. Pornhub uses a system from Apple to check user ages. But Ofcom thinks this new system may not work well. Websites with adult content must use strong age checks. Companies can pay a large fine if they do not follow the rules.

intermediate.headline: Pornhub's Age Checks Face Scrutiny from UK Regulator
intermediate.brief: Ofcom has launched an investigation into Aylo, Pornhub's owner, to see if the site's new age checks effectively prevent children from seeing adult material. The government body stated that Pornhub began using a new age verification process for some users, relying on Apple as a third party. Ofcom expressed concerns that Aylo might not have completed enough due diligence and testing before putting this new process into action, questioning its effectiveness. In a detailed statement, Aylo strongly defended its age verification method and promised full cooperation with the inquiry. Under the UK's Online Safety Act, websites hosting adult material must use highly effective age assurance to confirm users are over 18. As part of its investigation, Ofcom will examine how Aylo applies its age verification processes and if it carried out the necessary due diligence before implementation. However, Aylo claims that after trying various age-check methods in different markets, Apple's approach offers much stronger protection than any other currently available in the UK. The Online Safety Act gives Ofcom the authority to impose penalties on companies that don't comply, potentially up to £18 million or 10% of their annual global income.

advanced.headline: Pornhub Investigated Over Apple's Age Checks Efficacy
advanced.brief: Ofcom has initiated an investigation into Pornhub owner, Aylo, over whether the site's new age checks are effectively stopping children from accessing adult content. The regulator expressed concerns that Aylo "may not have conducted sufficient due diligence and testing" before implementing this new process, thereby questioning its potential efficacy in preventing children from viewing pornography. In a comprehensive statement to the BBC, Aylo vehemently defended its age verification methods, pledging full cooperation with the ongoing investigation. Under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA), platforms hosting pornographic material are mandated to employ highly effective age assurance to confirm users are over 18, although the specific method is left to the service's discretion. Aylo posits that, following extensive experimentation across diverse markets with various age-check methods, Apple's system offers "significantly stronger protection than any other age assurance method currently available in the UK market." The company further highlighted that Ofcom had previously praised Apple's technology as "a real win for children and families," using this as a point of commendation. Iain Corby, executive director of the Age Verification Providers Association, contended that an age-restricted site cannot solely rely on a mobile device-based system without demonstrating that children are definitively barred from accessing its content to the required standard. Aylo argues a system based on requiring individual pornographic sites to check users' ages simply drives users to riskier sites that do not adhere to Ofcom's regulations. The OSA empowers Ofcom to levy substantial penalties, potentially up to £18 million or 10% of a non-compliant company's annual global turnover, whichever sum is greater. This current probe represents the latest in a series of clashes between the regulatory body and one of the world's most extensively viewed adult platforms. In October 2025, Pornhub reported a dramatic plunge exceeding 75% in UK user traffic following the OSA's implementation of more stringent age checks. Some observers have speculated that users might have been circumventing these checks by employing Virtual Private Networks (VPNs) to bypass the restrictions. Earlier in January, Pornhub restricted access to its UK website, attributing this decision to the tougher verification requirements, permitting only existing account holders to view its content. Aylo initially asserted that the Act's updates, requiring age verification, had "not achieved its goal of protecting minors." However, in May, it announced a partial restoration of access for some UK Apple users who had verified their age via the company's most up-to-date iOS mobile operating system.
